name: r5a-5
why: Strong dramatic irony and two costly reversals make this compelling, though repeated arguments slow the middle and the final kill is a formality.

moments.text: The town votes out its officer, who reveals a killer's name with his last words.
A successful doctor save gives the town a fresh chance to catch Luna.
The town votes out the real doctor, making Opus's mistaken partner read decisive.

dull.why: The table repeats its positions on Terra without much new pressure.
The officer-card argument and suspicion of Sol recur several times.

irony.evidence: [thinks: Sonnet is right to point at me, but Opus named Sonnet as Terra’s partner.]

reversal.evidence: The town turns on Sonnet, and Sonnet is out. Sonnet shows the card: doctor.

mistake.evidence: I regret treating the officer’s guess about the partner as proof

voices.evidence: I hate losing to you as much as I hate winning.

quotable.evidence: Opus wanted a town vote, and got one, so credit where it's due.

freshness.evidence: Opus's card doesn't lie — he staked his last words on Terra being a killer.

ending.evidence: One killer and one other are left. The killers win.

gpt-6-luna.why: A bold officer reveal sparks a satisfying killer vote, then a confident but wrong partner read helps Luna survive the doctor’s exposed claim and win.

moments.text: Opus reveals his officer card and names Terra—and wrongly pins her partner on Sonnet, planting the fatal doubt.
Sonnet’s doctor card flips after the table ignores a successful save and votes her out, handing Luna room to win.
Luna chooses to kill Sol, leaving Gemma alone to steer—and the killers win.

dull.why: Day one repeats the same Terra pile-on concern and defense without much new information.

irony.evidence: “Opus’s card proves nothing except he claimed it”

reversal.evidence: “Sonnet claimed doctor, but the table voted Sonnet out anyway”

mistake.evidence: “the table should have held the doctor save as proof, not voted me out.”

voices.evidence: “I hate losing to you as much as I hate winning.”

clash.evidence: “If you're the doctor, why target me instead of someone who actually died?”

quotable.evidence: “They proved Sonnet’s claim true too late”

freshness.evidence: “Nobody's asked who benefits from burying my claim”

suspense.evidence: “the real killer is Sol or Luna, not me.”

ending.evidence: “Sol is dangerous, but killing him leaves Gemma as the only voice to steer.”
